sentences.text: The Food and Drug Directorate does not approve drugs sold on the Canadian market; instead, when a manufacturer submits a new drug application with data about the product, the information is reviewed by Food and Drug scientists and laboratory tests are performed, and when requirements for clinical effectiveness and other factors are established to the Directorate's satisfaction, a Notice of Compliance is issued allowing the drug to be released for sale.

It is impossible for the Food and Drug Directorate to carry out all the tests necessary to prove the safety of a drug, and it is the manufacturer's responsibility to ensure the safety of their drug for the purpose intended.

The Drug Safety, Quality and Efficacy Program includes the conduct of research into health hazards associated with drug use, establishment of safety and effectiveness standards and regulations, premarket evaluation of products, surveillance and enforcement of industry compliance with standards, and provision of information to health professionals and consumers regarding drug safety.

The Drugs Directorate's work in 1990 continued to focus on streamlining and enhancing Canada's system for examining the safety and efficacy of drugs, with goals to improve the safety and efficacy of drugs in Canada and provide timely and efficient market availability of new drugs.
